decisions.body:
Does the twelve-meeting corpus hold enough proposals to tell uptake from acknowledgement?
**By:** A. Researcher

Which source says speaking frequency is "well documented" for meetings like these?
**By:** A. Researcher

Framing power (lens: power and hierarchy) chosen; its statements are copied into the main canvas.
**By:** A. Researcher
**Why:** Every one of the twelve meetings records rank, so the framing can be tested on the whole corpus.
**Rejected:** rituals (lens: meeting routines and turn-taking); sense-making (lens: collective sense-making: "who hears whom")
decisions.why: Every one of the twelve meetings records rank, so the framing can be tested on the whole corpus.
decisions.rejected: rituals (lens: meeting routines and turn-taking); sense-making (lens: collective sense-making: "who hears whom")

decisions.body:
Speaking frequency is well documented; whether a proposal is taken up is not. [accepted, unverified]
**By:** A. Researcher
**Why:** The gap is uptake, not voice.
**Explained:** Earlier work counts who speaks; none of it asks whether a proposal is taken up, and that is what this study measures.
**Open at acceptance:** #1, #2
